## Donor cell (`type: dc`) {#sec-ch04-dc}

sources: OUTLINE.md chapter 4, scheme 4.3

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- The face state is the adjacent cell value: no stencil, no limiter.
- Switch: `type: dc`, and it is the YAML default.
- First order at the face, so first order in the flux divergence.
- Needs one ghost cell, which is why it is the only interpolant that runs on a block with `nghost = 1`.
:::

The simplest reconstruction there is, and the default the code falls back to when a deck names no type. The
left state of a face is the value of the cell to its left and the right state is the value of the cell to its
right, so the face carries a jump wherever the solution is not constant and the Riemann solver does all the
work.

### Derivation

A cell average equals the point value at the cell centre to $O(h^2)$, but the face is half a cell away from
either centre, so using the cell value at the face is wrong at $O(h)$. `[C7]` measures that directly: the face
error falls as $9.79\times10^{-2} \to 1.23\times10^{-2}$ over $n_1 = 32 \to 256$, a fitted order of 1.00.

First order at the face is the whole story of the scheme. It is also why donor cell is the useful control arm
in a test: any correction that claims to raise an order can be run against it and the difference is unambiguous.

### Numerical method

The implementation is a copy, at [`interpolation.hpp:88-105`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interpolation.hpp#L88-L105): `left` and `right` take the
neighbouring cell value with no arithmetic at all. Because the stencil is one cell wide, the ghost width the
framework computes from it is the smallest of any interpolant, and donor cell is the only type that runs on a
block with a single ghost layer.

### Limits

1. **First order everywhere.** Nothing in the scheme adapts: smooth regions are reconstructed as badly as
   discontinuities. A deck that leaves `type` unset gets this scheme, which is rarely what is wanted for a
   production run and is easy to miss because no warning is printed.
